S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

patient_info.stressor: Kimberly Brady’s promotion into a part-time safety-training role after years of reliable factory work was a proud achievement, but it also brought public recognition, training demonstrations, and photographs for the company newsletter and senior-center workshops. In that new spotlight, she became increasingly focused on a slight perceived flaw in her hands and face, checking herself repeatedly before presentations and comparing her appearance with coworkers and friends at art and book-club events. Although she continued working and volunteering, the added preparation made her slower to start classes, more likely to avoid being photographed, and less spontaneous in the social activities that had helped her since widowhood. At an annual primary-care appointment, she raised the issue herself because it was interfering with her transition plans, and her physician arranged a psychiatric referral.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I came in because since I started helping with the safety trainings, I can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out, and then I start thinking my face looks crooked in the newsletter photos even though other people say they don’t see it.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before a class or a senior-center workshop, I’ll check the bathroom mirror a few times, put lotion on my hands, turn my face different ways, and sometimes ask a coworker if I look all right, which makes me run a little behind but I still get myself there.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: It hasn’t stopped me from working or volunteering, but I’m slower getting ready for trainings and I’ve started ducking out of photos or hesitating before social events I used to enjoy more easily.
